passages.note: His own words back leasing a prison to house federal immigration detainees; this is enforcement-capacity funding, which the annex says shows the enforcement side only (direction-only), not who is removed.
His own words back a grant funding immigration-training costs for law enforcement personnel; this is general enforcement-resourcing, not a statement of who should be deported.

His own words frame a detainer/information-sharing requirement (county facilities must supply arrestee info to ICE) as supporting deportation efforts; the annex treats a state-local cooperation requirement as the local-immigration question, not the removal-scope question.

rows.reasoning: His own quotes back federal enforcement infrastructure (leasing Marana Prison to hold 'dangerous criminal illegal aliens') and a detainer/information-sharing requirement he frames as supporting 'the federal government's deportation efforts,' both of which show the pro-enforcement side without matching any rung's specific scope clause (e.g. 'only... convicted of serious violent crimes' or 'all... starting with those who have criminal records'). SB 1299's training-grant quotes are adjacent, addressing enforcement resourcing rather than who is deported.
